note: The shipped pack is generated by the `elevenlabs` block (`npm run narration:generate`) in the owner-chosen ElevenLabs voice. The `kokoro` block (`npm run narration:generate:kokoro`) is the keyless local fallback that produced the earlier British bf_emma pack; the top-level model/voice/instructions drive the optional OpenAI path (`npm run narration:generate:openai`). All three read the one `cues` map below, keyed by stable cue id (the id is the filename).
instructions: Speak in a natural British English accent, like a warm, unhurried parent guiding one curious five-year-old. Calm, natural and friendly, never announcer-like or sing-song. Use short pauses between ideas, clear consonants, and a gently excited tone. Do not rush. Do not add words that are not in the script.

cues.arrival-sun: We made it to the Sun! It is our nearest star. It gives Earth light and warmth. There is no ground to land on, so we look from space.
cues.arrival-earth: We made it to Earth! This is our home, seen from space. Tap a picture to play.
cues.arrival-moon: We made it to the Moon! There is no air or weather here. Tap a picture to play.
cues.arrival-mars: We made it to Mars! Its red dust is full of rust. Tap a picture to play.
cues.discovery-earth-sahara: This is the Sahara! It is the biggest hot desert in the world, and it is enormous even from space.
cues.discovery-earth-amazon: This is the Amazon rainforest! More kinds of animals live here than anywhere else on Earth.
cues.discovery-earth-nightside: This is Earth's night side! Those tiny glows are towns and cities full of people.
cues.discovery-moon-tranquility: This is where Apollo 11 landed! The astronauts' footprints are still there, because there is no wind or rain.
cues.discovery-moon-tycho: This is Tycho! A crashing space rock splashed those bright streaks of dust across the Moon.
cues.discovery-moon-farside: This is the Moon's far side! People never saw this side until a spacecraft flew around it.
cues.discovery-mars-olympus: This is Olympus Mons! It is the biggest volcano in the whole solar system.
cues.discovery-mars-marineris: This is Valles Marineris! This giant crack is longer than Australia is wide.
cues.discovery-mars-elysium: This is Elysium Mons! This volcano would still be twice as tall as Earth's tallest mountain.
cues.toy-moon: Tap Jump! On the Moon you jump much higher than on Earth.
cues.toy-saturn: Drag a planet into the bath. Which one floats?
cues.toy-mars: Tap a rock, and the rover drives there. Mars is so far away, it takes a while.
cues.toy-moonlight: You can see where moonlight comes from.
cues.toy-sun: You can drag the rocket far away.
cues.sunstar-start: Up close, the Sun is huge.
cues.sunstar-earth: From Earth, the Sun looks this big.
cues.sunstar-neptune: From Neptune it is a very bright star.
cues.sunstar-far: Far, far away the Sun is a star. The other stars are suns too.
cues.spin-earth: Watch the sunlight move while Earth turns. The bright side is day, and the dark side is night.
cues.discovery-earth-lakes: These are the Great Lakes! Five huge lakes joined together, holding more fresh water than almost anywhere on Earth.
cues.discovery-earth-himalaya: These are the Himalayas! The tallest mountains on Earth are down there, and they are still getting taller.
cues.discovery-earth-reef: This is the Great Barrier Reef! It is the biggest reef in the world, and tiny animals built every bit of it.
cues.spin-moon: Watch day come to the Moon. Its days are very long: two weeks of sunshine, then two weeks of dark.
cues.discovery-moon-procellarum: This is the Ocean of Storms! There is no water in it at all. It is a huge flat plain of old cooled rock.
cues.discovery-moon-crisium: This is the Sea of Crises! A gigantic rock smashed in here, and melted rock filled the hole right up.
cues.discovery-moon-orientale: This is Orientale! It really is shaped like a bullseye, with rings of mountains inside rings of mountains.
cues.spin-mars: Watch day come to Mars. A day here is almost exactly as long as a day on Earth.
cues.discovery-mars-hellas: This is Hellas! It is a hole so deep that Earth's biggest mountain would fit right inside it.
cues.discovery-mars-jezero: This is Jezero crater! A robot landed here with a tiny helicopter, the first one ever to fly on another world.
cues.discovery-mars-gale: This is Gale crater! A robot the size of a car has been driving around down here, drilling into the rocks.
cues.spin-saturn: Watch day come to Saturn. It spins so fast that a whole day here is only about ten hours long.
cues.arrival-saturn: We made it to Saturn! This is the planet with the beautiful rings. Tap a picture to play.
cues.discovery-saturn-rings: These are the rings! They are billions of pieces of ice and rock going round Saturn, from tiny crumbs to lumps as big as a house.
cues.discovery-saturn-hexagon: This is the six-sided storm! Right at the top of Saturn is a giant cloud shaped like a hexagon, with six straight sides.
cues.discovery-saturn-storm: This is a giant storm! Saturn's storms are far bigger than any on Earth, and they can rumble on for months.
cues.discovery-saturn-division: This is the big gap in the rings! One of Saturn's moons keeps sweeping it clear, over and over.
cues.discovery-saturn-jet: This is Saturn's fastest wind! Round the middle it never stops blowing, quicker than a jet plane.
cues.discovery-saturn-bands: These are the stripes! Each stripe is a band of cloud, and every one races round Saturn at its own speed.
cues.spin-intro-earth: Watch. Earth is turning. That is day, and that is night.
cues.spin-invite-earth: You can turn Earth. Tap the little globe.
cues.home-first: Tap the Moon. We will fly there.
cues.home-earth: You can fly to Earth. Tap it.
cues.home-moon: You can fly to the Moon. Tap it.
cues.home-mars: You can fly to Mars. Tap it.
cues.home-saturn: You can fly to Saturn. Tap it.
cues.home-any: You can tap any world to fly there.
cues.fly-home: Back home. You can pick another world.
cues.spin-invite-moon: You can turn the Moon. Tap the globe.
cues.spin-invite-mars: You can turn Mars. Tap the globe.
cues.spin-invite-saturn: You can turn Saturn. Tap the globe.
cues.day-night-start: Turn Earth. Take your house into night.
cues.day-night-night: Night time! The lights come on. Can you bring back morning?
cues.day-night-moon: Morning again! You can fly to the Moon next.
cues.day-night-done: Morning again! You can keep turning Earth.
cues.home-sun: You can fly to the Sun.
cues.home-nudge-sun: Tap the Sun to fly there.
